metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Virginia (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Ex.

description: Virginia has a statewide sales tax; bullion and legal-tender coins are exempt only on invoices of $1,000+ that meet state guidance. Jewelry is taxed. Verify.

What's covered by the exemption
Gold, silver, and platinum bullion and legal-tender coins — on orders of $1,000+. The current rule is scheduled to sunset on June 30, 2026 unless renewed.
How they decide what counts as bullion
Order has to total $1,000 or more, the metal must be at least 90% pure, and the price has to be based on weight and purity — not rarity. Rule extended through June 30, 2026; verify before relying on it.
What's NOT covered
Orders under $1,000, items under 90% purity, jewelry, artwork, and rarity-priced collectibles.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Virginia.
Is gold or silver bullion taxable in Virginia?
+
It depends on the transaction. Virginia’s guidance indicates the sale can be exempt only if the invoice is at least $1,000 and the item is qualifying bullion.
What is Virginia’s threshold for tax-free bullion purchases?
+
Virginia’s guidance uses a $1,000 minimum invoice threshold for the exemption on qualifying bullion and legal-tender coins.
What bullion qualifies for the Virginia exemption?
+
State guidance references items that are at least 90% precious metal with value based on mass and purity, and it applies to qualifying bullion and legal-tender coins.
Are numismatic or collector coins exempt in Virginia?
+
Not always. They may be exempt only if they qualify under Virginia’s bullion/legal-tender guidance and the invoice meets the $1,000 threshold.
Is jewelry taxed in Virginia?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable under Virginia’s sales tax rules.
